# Clutch — machining sheet (generated by mechanical/clutch/clutch.py)

All dimensions mm. **Bold** = critical for concentricity or the magnetic gaps: turn these in ONE chucking.
Concentricity budget: every bold diameter ≤ 0.03 TIR to its part's reference bore. After assembly, indicate the
rotor OD and the output shaft: ≤ 0.05 TIR each, or the 0.3 mm hub gap and the tooth mesh suffer.
Magnetic parts: low-carbon steel (1018/1020/12L14), anneal after machining if possible. Never 300-series stainless.

| Feature | Dimension | Tolerance / note |
|---|---|---|
| OD | **Ø80.0** | h7 (cover spigot fits over it) |
| Length | 20.0 | ±0.05 — sets the 0.3 mm rotor face gap |
| Motor pilot recess (back) | **Ø38.1 (measure your motor) × 2.0 deep** | slide fit on the pilot, ≤0.02 play; the model shows +0.2 |
| Inner pole bore | **Ø19.2** through | concentric with OD and pilot within 0.03 |
| Coil cavity | Ø28.0 … Ø54.0, 15.0 deep from the front | |
| Back plate | 5.0 thick | |
| Motor screws | 4× Ø5.5 thru on 47.14 square, c'bore Ø9 from front to z=6 | M5×30 SHCS + nuts behind the motor flange |
| Coil leads | Ø3.2 thru at r=20.5 + 3.2×1.5 groove on the back face | |
| Cover screws | 6× M4 tapped radial, every 60°, 12.0 from the back face (motor side) | |

| Feature | Dimension | Tolerance / note |
|---|---|---|
| Hub OD | **Ø18.6** × 18.1 long | runs in the Ø19.2 bore: 0.3 radial gap, keep runout < 0.05. Starts 2.2 above the motor flange, clear of the 1.6 pilot |
| Shaft bore | **Ø10 H7**, depth = **measured shaft length − 2.2 ± 0.03** (model: 18.8) | round; Loctite 641 on the D-shaft. The depth sets the 0.3 face gap |
| Retaining screw | Ø3.4 thru + c'bore Ø5.8 × 3.2 from the front | M3×8 SHCS (3.0 head, sits 0.2 below the pole face) into the tapped motor shaft end (drill Ø2.5 × 8, tap M3) |
| Face disc | **Ø76.0** × 5.6 thick | back face sits 0.3 from the housing front; front face = pole face |
| Banana slots | 3 × 112° arcs, r 19.0 … 22.0, through (8° bridges) | CNC, Ø3 end mill |
| Tooth ring | r 32.0 … 38.0, 30 teeth (12.0° pitch), flank 30° from axis | roots 0.5 below the pole face; tips 0.80 above the roots (0.9 profile, tips truncated 0.1); see teeth notes |

## Other parts
- Output shaft: Ø12 h6 ground rod × 78. Flats 0.6 deep: × 22 at the pulley end, × 10 under the hub boss. DIN 471-12 groove (Ø11.5 × 1.1) at 52.6 from its motor-side end, outboard of the outer bearing.
- Leaf springs: 3× 0.3 mm blue spring-steel shim, 14 wide with full-round ends, holes Ø3.3 at 27.7 centres. **Flat when released**; engaged they bend 1.1 mm (≈25 N total).
- Spacers: 3× Ø7 × 2.40, Ø3.3 hole (steel or brass), between the armature and the strap.
- Bearing stack (front to back): circlip, outer 6001, spacer tube Ø27.95/Ø25 × 17.0 (outer races), inner 6001, circlip. The inner bearing locates the shaft: a stepped spacer Ø15/Ø12 × 4.5 between the hub boss and its inner race, the DIN 471-12 circlip outboard of the outer bearing. Grind or shim the stepped spacer so the springs are flat with the armature resting on them.
- Coil: ~850 turns 0.32 mm (AWG 28) enamelled Cu on a bobbin Ø28.6…Ø53.4 × 14.5; ≈24 Ω. Leads out through the back plate.
- Bearings: 2× 6001-2RS (k6 shaft / H7 bore: tighter on the rotating inner ring). Screws: 4× M5×30 + nuts (motor), 6× M4×8 (cover), 3× M3×6 low-head DIN 7984 (hub end, from the armature side), 3× M3×6 SHCS (armature end, through the hub access holes), 1× M3×8 (rotor), 2× M5×6 set screws (hub), 4× M5×20 (module to the feed-unit plate).
- Coil leads: sleeve them through the back plate, and pot the winding in the cavity (epoxy) so it cannot chafe or move.
- Coil cavity: turn it with a grooving or boring bar from the front; it's a blind annulus 15.0 deep.

## Teeth
- 30 radial teeth, true angular profile: equal tip and root lands, flanks 30° from the axis at the mean radius.
- Engaged pole gap 0.15, stroke 1.1 -> released gap 1.25.
- Tips truncated 0.1 mm on both rings: the flanks carry the load and the 0.1 tip/root clearance means a tip can never bottom out.
- Machine both rings with the same CAM program and tool, in the same setup orientation, then lap them together.
- Radial teeth have a constant angle, so the flank twists slightly with radius: rough with an end mill, finish the flanks with a ball end mill.
- Flanks: 3D finishing with a small ball end mill (Ø1–2) or a chamfer mill whose half-angle equals the flank angle
  (30° flank -> 60° chamfer mill / V-bit; set `flank_deg = 45` for a standard 90° chamfer mill — the cam-out force
  then rises ~1.8x, so expect ~1.3x more hold current; re-calibrate per design.md §7.4).
